gap: No result ChatGPT got states what each inverter burns just by staying on. Over 24 hours that comes to about 1.56 kWh/day (569 kWh/yr) for the EG4 FlexBOSS21, 2.16 kWh/day (788 kWh/yr) for the Sol-Ark 15K-2P, 1.44–1.68 kWh/day for the EG4 18kPV, 1.2 kWh/day for the EG4 6000XP and 2.59 kWh/day for the Sol-Ark 18K. Off-grid, the Sol-Ark 15K uses about 219 kWh more per year than the FlexBOSS21 just sitting idle.
standout_why: I checked three cited pages. ecosolarkits.com/blogs/guides/eg4-vs-sol-ark works out $/kW of battery-only output and battery amps at full load. ecosolarkits.com/blogs/guides/split-phase-inverter-explained works out $/kW of continuous output and battery current. liveoffthegrid.com/specs/inverters has $/W and charger amps. None of them gives an idle or no-load draw, or turns it into kWh per day or per year. So the $/kW angle is already covered and the energy lost to idle draw is not.
decides: It backs EG4 FlexBOSS21 and EG4 18kPV over Sol-Ark 15K for off-grid or battery-heavy buyers. They are cheaper per kW, and they also draw about 20–30 W less at idle, which saves roughly 0.5–0.7 kWh every day from the battery bank. For a grid-tied owner it doesn't change the pick, because the grid covers that small loss. EG4 6000XP has the lowest idle draw (about 1.2 kWh/day) for small off-grid builds.
